html:
The Kingdom of Georgia was a medieval Christian monarchy in the Caucasus, founded around 1008 when Bagrat III united the western and eastern Georgian lands. It is shown here in 1000 and 1100.

It was ruled by the Bagrationi dynasty and stood between Byzantium, the Islamic world and the steppe. In the late 11th century the Seljuk Turks overran much of it. David IV, called the Builder, turned that around: he reformed the army, settled Kipchak warriors as soldiers, crushed a much larger Seljuk force at the Battle of Didgori in 1121 and took back Tbilisi in 1122, making it his capital.

The golden age peaked under Queen Tamar, who ruled from 1184 to 1213 over lands and vassals from the Black Sea to the Caspian. The poet Shota Rustaveli wrote The Knight in the Panther's Skin at her court. The Mongol invasions from the 1220s broke Georgian power. Later wars and plague wore it down, and by about 1490 it had split into three kingdoms and several principalities.
